gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Commanding from the first glance, Bloody stacks big round lowercase bowls into a loud headline. Noto Sans Tagalog quietly wins on its middle zone, which dominates each line, and its curves keep generous gaps.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its blunt, commanding face. Noto Sans Tagbanwa works in open curves with clear gaps, its lowercase filling most of the height, which keeps it clean and modern.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads approachable, its ink strokes tapering out before they touch and its capitals barely stepping up. Bloody supplies the shout while that text stays quiet beneath it.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Bloody brings big round lowercase bowls and a commanding swagger. Noto Sans Tai Tham crowds its chalk-board lowercase up toward the capital line, yet each c stays visibly open, so paragraphs glide along.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Loud and round, Bloody swells its lowercase into big bowls. Noto Sans Tai Viet mixes short ascenders, pulled-back terminals and a tall x-height, so paragraphs read approachable and steady.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-takri: Big and round, Bloody takes the top line while Noto Sans Takri sets a high-waisted lowercase of generously unclosed curves. One shouts, the other keeps the sans-serif text moving.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Contemporary in feel, Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified without changing size, its terminals stopping far from the stem. Bloody growls overhead with its round bowls; the sans-serif text carries the detail.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tamil-sup: Round bowls, big and loud, define Bloody at a glance. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement is the quieter partner, round forms like open parentheses under a middle band so tall each line looks stocky.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Approachable at once, Noto Sans Tangsa opens its round letters wide, with short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies. And Bloody does what it does best: shout, in big round bowls.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tc: Bloody does its best shouting through big round lowercase bowls. Noto Sans TC handles the quiet work, with large open counters and curves that flare outward instead of curling in.
